title: How to find a will after someone dies (US)
dek: Search likely custodians, preserve every version and ask the right court about depositing an original, without assuming a found will gives you authority.
metaDescription: Search likely custodians, preserve every version and ask the right court about depositing an original, without assuming a found will gives you authority.

paragraphs: To find a will after someone dies in the US, check the person's lawful paper storage, ask the drafting attorney or successor firm, and contact the probate court serving their last residence. Ask about a safe-deposit box through the bank's deceased-customer process. Keep a search record, preserve every version and check local deposit requirements promptly.

You may have heard only that the will is with a lawyer, without knowing which lawyer or whether the document at home is the signed original. Treat that as a lead rather than an answer. This guide concerns finding and preserving evidence; it cannot determine whether a document is valid or which state's law governs a disputed estate.

body.heading: Search without changing the evidence
items: Ask the person coordinating the estate whether an original, copy, later amendment or attorney contact is already known. Agree who will record the search.
Check accessible files, document boxes and other places you are entitled to search. Keep papers together and note where each document was found.
Contact the drafting attorney or firm through independently verified details. Ask whether it holds an original, only a copy, or a record of transfer to another custodian.
If a lawyer retired or a firm closed, ask about the successor practice or file custodian. A local bar association may help identify the correct enquiry route.
Ask the probate clerk whether a will or estate case has already been lodged, and whether local law provides for depositing wills before death. No result is not proof that no will exists.
If a bank box or locked storage is involved, ask for the specific lawful access procedure. Do not assume possession of a key grants access to the contents.
Photograph or copy found documents for reference while preserving originals intact. Record custody and ask the court about the required next step.

body.heading: Ask about the deadline early, not after the whole search
paragraphs: Finding every possible version can take time, but a custodian's duty to deposit an original may already have started. [Florida section 732.901](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0700-0799/0732/Sections/0732.901.html) requires the custodian to deposit the will with the court having venue within ten days after receiving information of the death. That is a Florida example, not a national deadline.

California court guidance describes a different deadline: thirty days after learning of the death for delivering the original, subject to the applicable rules. Ask the relevant clerk for current instructions, required accompanying information and whether there are related copy-delivery duties. Depositing a will and applying to administer an estate are separate acts. Do not postpone the first because you are not ready for the second.

body.heading: Record what you found, not what you assume
rows: A lawyer or proposed plan existed.
Whether any valid version was later executed.
A copy of a signed document
A version and possible custodian can be identified.
Where the original is and whether it was changed or revoked.
An original document has been located.
Validity, later amendments and applicable deposit or probate requirements.
A document or proceeding was filed there.
Its status, completeness and effect on the present estate.

body.heading: Invented example: a copy and a later document
paragraphs: A niece finds a photocopy dated several years earlier. The firm named on it says the original was returned to the client. She records that answer and asks the bank about lawful access to a box mentioned in correspondence. A later signed document is eventually found through the permitted process.

She keeps both versions, the firm's response and the discovery dates. She does not destroy the earlier copy or decide that a later date alone proves the newer paper governs. A probate attorney reviews the documents, including whether an amendment changes only part of an earlier will. The example is about evidence handling, not a rule for choosing between wills.

body.heading: A will does not appoint you by discovery
paragraphs: Read who is nominated, but do not assume that person can immediately withdraw money or sell property. [New York Courts explains fiduciary appointment](https://www.nycourts.gov/help/when-someone-dies/fiduciary-estate): appointment and duties are handled through the court process there. Your state may have a different procedure or a small-estate alternative. Finding the will does not make the finder the representative.

Do not use a deceased person's login or power-of-attorney paperwork as a shortcut to search private accounts. Ask the institution and an estate adviser what access is permitted after death. Beneficiary designations, jointly owned property and trusts may follow routes outside the will, so the will itself is not necessarily an inventory of everything the person owned.

items.line: I am trying to locate the original will for [name], who died on [date]. Please tell me your verification requirements, whether you hold a document, and whether your records identify another custodian.
I have located a document described as a will. Which court has the deposit process, what deadline applies to the custodian, and how should the original and any amendments be delivered?

body.heading: If no original appears, or relatives disagree
paragraphs: Keep the search log and seek advice about the next process. A missing original does not automatically mean there was never a will, and a photocopy is not automatically useless. Local evidence rules determine what can be proved. Similarly, do not assume an informal handwritten note is either valid or invalid without advice.

Escalate promptly if someone refuses to produce a known document, pages appear missing or altered, property is being distributed, or there are competing claims about capacity or pressure. Do not confront a disputed document by writing on it or destroying another version. Preserve what you have and ask about protective steps.

If the estate proceeds without a valid will, the applicable intestacy and appointment rules determine the route. They are not a family vote about what seems fair. Use [the US executor guide](/guides/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to) to understand the distinction between locating documents and accepting estate administration.

items.q: Can I search for the will online?
items.a: You can check the relevant court's official records and any locally available deposit or registry process, but no universal US website contains every private will. A negative search does not prove absence. Combine court enquiries with the home-paperwork and attorney-custodian search, keeping dates and responses.

items.q: Does the newest document always win?
items.a: Not simply because its date is later. Validity, amendments, revocation and the interaction between documents can matter. Preserve all versions and ask a qualified estate attorney to assess them. Do not tear up an older will or mark it cancelled based only on your own reading.

items.q: Can I open a bank box if I have its key?
items.a: A key is not a universal authorization. The bank and applicable state law determine who can access a deceased customer's box, what evidence is required and what may be removed. Ask specifically about a will-search procedure and keep any bank record of the access and document handling.
